subject: Hightide POC: prefetched K/V eviction during burst — SDK escape hatch and rollback policy
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@hightide.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-05T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hightide POC - KV eviction observed during burst demo

Hi Aisha,

Quick note from our session this morning — during the 11:00 demo load test we saw the model responses start to truncate mid-stream (~t+18s) and then subsequent requests for the same session started returning short / low-quality completions. Attaching the server-side logs we captured (hightide_demo_logs.txt).

What I can tell from the logs: there are repeated cache miss spikes followed by explicit K/V eviction events; eviction timestamps line up with burst spikes when we ramp to 250 concurrent sessions. We suspect the prefetch window might be growing unexpectedly per session and then eviction is thrashing the KV cache.

Repro steps we used:
- Start 250 concurrent websocket sessions, keep prompts ~1.2k tokens
- Enable client prefetch (default SDK behavior)
- After ~90s, observe stream truncation on ~3-5% sessions

Can you loop in runtime/SDK folks? This is blocking our next demo with procurement next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Oliver
CTO, Hightide AI

Attachment: hightide_demo_logs.txt (text, 86KB)

Subject: Fwd: Hightide POC - KV eviction observed during burst demo (triage request + field ask)

Forwarding logs from Hightide — they hit a reproducible failure pattern during a high-concurrency demo. Oliver included the logs; attaching their repro trace too (prefetch_repro_trace.txt).

Ask: can runtime/SDK analyze whether client prefetch + session affinity could trigger uncontrolled growth of per-session prefetch buffers, leading to eviction thrash? If we can get a short-term mitigation, customer demo is next Tue (2027-09-07).

Proposed short-term mitigations (please comment):
- SDK escape hatch header / flag to disable prefetch on a per-session basis (e.g. x-redwood-prefetch: off)
- Conservative default PREFETCH_WINDOW_MAX in SDK to cap per-session prefetch size
- Runtime canary that disables prefetch routing for a % of traffic from this account until a fix is in place

Please reply with: 1) triage findings in 24h, 2) whether an escape hatch is feasible in 48h, 3) rollback/canary plan. Oliver — I’ll keep you posted but want internal alignment first.

--

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-09-06T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hightide POC - KV eviction observed during burst demo (initial triage)

Quick triage notes after an initial pass on the logs and repro trace:
- Pattern looks like per-session prefetch queues growing beyond expected bounds. Eviction events correlate with large contiguous allocations coming from sessions marked as sticky to the same worker.
- Two likely contributors: 1) SDK is prefetching aggressively for long prompts (we saw up to 128-step prefetch windows in traces), 2) a session affinity/regeneration bug allows stale session handles to accumulate on the worker, preventing early cache eviction.

Short-term mitigation options:
1) SDK escape hatch header (fast): implement x-redwood-prefetch: off which the server will honor and bypass prefetch routing for the session. Server-side change is small (check header before enqueuing prefetch work). SDK change: expose a config flag to set header per session. Estimated turnaround: runtime change ~1 business day for patch + QA, SDK change ~1 day (Typescript + Py SDK) for 2.1.0 release.
2) SDK cap (fast): introduce PREFETCH_WINDOW_MAX default to 32 steps; this can be shipped in the SDK sooner but is a behavioral change for all customers — prefer as opt-in for now.
3) Longer fix: address session handle leak (requires deeper runtime work).

Proposed immediate plan:
- Implement escape hatch header and ship in a patch to hosted runtime (can be toggled via rollout flag).
- Ship SDK 2.1.0 with an opt-in config and a clear note in changelog.
- Run a canary for Hightide with escape hatch off by default, then flip to off for their traffic if they want to force-disable prefetch for the demo.

I filed an internal ticket: JIRA INF-4829 with repro trace and earliest suggested patch. Drive folder with repro: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cHTD-repro.

Risk notes: disabling prefetch increases latency for some use cases and may increase token/compute cost. Must communicate to customer.

— Logan

logan@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Hightide POC - KV eviction observed during burst demo (canary + ops ask)

Thanks Logan — operational notes and proposed canary checklist attached.

Canary proposal (summary):
- Canary scope: Hosted runtime region us-west1, target Hightide account traffic only.
- Canary size: 2% traffic -> 10% -> 50% over a 24–48h window if metrics look stable.
- Metrics to watch: stream truncation rate, per-session memory allocation, eviction rate, p50/p95 token latency, cost delta per 1k tokens.
- Rollback triggers: >0.5% increase in truncation OR >30% increase in eviction events OR >20% latency regression at p95.

Checklist attached: canary_run_checklist.md (stub). Ops work: need a short runtime patch to honor x-redwood-prefetch header and a feature rollout flag in the control plane. QA: small internal load test matching Hightide repro (we can reuse their trace). Estimated end-to-end for patch+canary: 36–48 hours if we prioritize.

Also product note: we should not change global PREFETCH_WINDOW default without explicit product approval — opt-in SDK flag + header escape hatch is less surprising for customers. Karthik / Product, please confirm.

— Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: canary_run_checklist.md (markdown, 4KB)

Date: 2027-09-07T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hightide POC - action plan for Tuesday demo (summary & ask)

Oliver — thanks for the quick repro logs. Internal team confirmed a likely interaction between client prefetch and per-session affinity leading to KV eviction thrash. Proposed immediate plan:

1) We will ship a runtime patch to honor a per-session header (x-redwood-prefetch: off) and publish an SDK 2.1.0 opt-in config to set that header. Patch + opt-in SDK can be completed and rolled to a small canary within ~36–48 hours.
2) Ops will run a controlled canary scoped to your account starting at 2% traffic and evaluate the metrics (see checklist). If you want us to force-disable prefetch for all your sessions during the Tuesday demo we can apply the header for your account via a temporary routing override — this will increase latencies slightly but should avoid truncation.

Please reply with:
- Permission to run the canary on your account starting Tue 09/07 at 17:00 PT (we expect to complete the patch earlier that day).
- A short sample prompt set (2–3 prompts of the long-doc flow) that you consider critical to reproduce so we can validate before the demo.

We’ll keep the rollout constrained and provide a rollback plan. Thanks — we’ll prioritize.

Best,
Aisha
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
